objectives: Demonstrate initial-bl recognition, decoding, spelling, rime knowledge, sentence comprehension and fluency.
Complete a balanced 15-item diagnostic with independent responses.
Use response evidence to identify the weakest component.
concepts: A diagnostic samples several taught skills rather than repeating only one item type.
An error pattern helps identify a specific next teaching step.
Accuracy and meaning matter alongside smooth connected reading.
Below-threshold performance routes to targeted remediation, not automatic advancement.

definitions.definition: A short assessment used to identify strengths and specific learning needs.
The minimum score required to advance to the next learning cycle.
Reading accurately and smoothly while keeping the meaning of the text.
Responses grouped by skill area to show where support is needed.

workedExamples.prompt: A learner reads block as bock.
workedExamples.solution: Record a decoding error involving the /l/ in the initial blend.

workedExamples.prompt: A learner spells black as bak.
workedExamples.solution: Record an encoding error because l and the taught ck spelling are missing.

workedExamples.prompt: A learner reads accurately but cannot answer where the blob is.
workedExamples.solution: Check sentence comprehension and text-evidence use, not only decoding.

commonMistakes: Using one missed item to label every skill as weak.
Scoring speed instead of accurate, meaningful reading.
Reusing the same questions during remediation reassessment.
keyTakeaways: Sample recognition, decoding, encoding, word families, comprehension and fluency.
Use the response pattern to choose a targeted next step.
At or above 80% meets the defined mastery threshold.
Below 80% routes to targeted remediation and fresh reassessment.
revisionPoints: Decode the vowel and ending, not only the onset.
Use sentence evidence for literal questions.
Read accurately, smoothly and for meaning.
studyMaterial.weakTopicRevision: If diagnostic accuracy is below 80%, identify the weakest component, teach it explicitly, practise with guided feedback, and reassess using fresh items.
outcomes: Identify a weak skill component from the response pattern.
Use accurate reading and text evidence to demonstrate readiness.

activities.name: Complete the balanced bl-cycle diagnostic.
steps: Read and answer all 15 items independently.

steps: Name the specific skill needing support.

basic.prompt: Name a word that begins with bl.
What are the first two sounds in black?
What is the rime in blank?

conceptual.prompt: What is the purpose of a diagnostic?
conceptual.answer: To identify strengths and specific learning needs.

conceptual.prompt: What score meets 80% on 15 one-mark questions?

conceptual.answer: Smooth reading is useful only when the words and meaning remain accurate.

application.prompt: If block is read as bock, which component needs support?
If black is spelled bak, which component needs support?
What route applies to a score below 80%?

higherOrderThinking.prompt: Why should you review a pattern of errors instead of one error?
higherOrderThinking.answer: A pattern gives stronger evidence about the skill needing support.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: How can a learner show sentence comprehension?
higherOrderThinking.answer: Answer from the sentence and point to the words that support it.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: Why must reassessment use fresh items?
higherOrderThinking.answer: To check transfer rather than memorised answers.

mixedReview.prompt: Which two phonemes make the initial blend bl?
What is a safe next step after a diagnostic below threshold?
mixedReview.answer: Teach the weakest component, practise and reassess.

mixedReview.prompt: What are the six sampled components?
mixedReview.answer: Sound recognition, decoding, encoding, word families, comprehension and fluency

questions.question: Which word begins with the blend bl?
What are the first two phonemes in black?
Which word ends with the rime -ess?
What is the onset in blank?
Which word has a different initial blend from black, blank and blink?
Read: “The black block is on the mat.” What is on the mat?
Read: “A blob is on the block.” Where is the blob?
If block is read as bock, what should the reader do?
options: Add a vowel between b and l

questions.question: Which is the best description of fluent reading?
options: Accurate, smooth reading that keeps the meaning
Guessing each word from the first letter

questions.question: Which event order matches the controlled passage?
options: Ben has a block; a blob is on it; Ben dabs the blob
Ben dabs the blob; Ben gets a block; the blob appears
The blob leaves; Ben has a rag; Ben finds a block
Ben has a rag; the block is wet; Ben gets a blob

questions.question: If a learner scores 10 out of 15, what is the next route?
options: Targeted remediation because the score is below 80%
Advance because 10 is more than half
Repeat the same questions until memorised

answerKeys.explanation: Blush begins bl and has the rime -ush.
The onset is the initial consonant group bl.
Brick begins br; the others begin bl.
The sentence states that the black block is on the mat.
The phrase on the block gives the location.
The /l/ must be kept in the blend.
Fluency includes accuracy, smoothness and comprehension.
The first sequence follows the stated passage order.
Ten out of fifteen is below the 12/15 mastery threshold.
